errors.text: The proposed mechanism reverses the key defect trend: it attributes the 900–1200 K transition to stacking-fault and partial-dislocation proliferation, whereas the target describes rapid lattice disorder accompanied by substantial dislocation-density reduction and a shift away from stacking-fault-mediated deformation.
The 600 K behavior is assigned to dislocation forest hardening rather than the observed reduction in dislocation density associated with increased elastic modulus.

FCC-to-HCP martensitic transformation is elevated to the primary cause of friction and softening without target-specific evidence; increased HCP atom count can also represent stacking-fault environments and does not by itself establish a bulk phase transformation.

The falsification rule mainly tests whether HCP transformation is necessary, rather than cleanly distinguishing thermally induced disorder from indentation-driven mechanical annealing or defect annihilation.
